passage:
Wednesday night
Hafsa from final year sat with me at lunch again. She said I'm "so much more mature than the other first-years", that I have "leader energy", that she could tell the first time she saw me. I felt ten feet tall.
Then she told me about the "opportunity": sell some products, bring in two friends, pay a joining fee, "and you'll earn more than your parents". She said, "Someone like you won't overthink it."
The weird part: I wanted to say yes just so I wouldn't seem rude after all those compliments. Saying "let me think" felt like slapping her.
But I did say it. Tonight I'm asking my brother, and I'll look the company up on a consumer forum before I pay anything. If it's real, it'll still be real on Monday.
Amandeep

qa.q: What did Hafsa say Amandeep has?
qa.a: "Leader energy", and she said Amandeep is "so much more mature than the other first-years".

qa.q: Why did saying "let me think" feel so hard for Amandeep?
qa.a: Amandeep felt flattered and warm, then awkward, because after so many compliments disagreeing felt rude, like slapping Hafsa.

qa.q: What protective steps does Amandeep plan?
qa.a: Amandeep will pause, ask the brother tonight, and look the company up on a consumer forum before paying anything.

qa.q: What does Hafsa's "Someone like you won't overthink it" suggest about what she wants?
qa.a: It suggests she wants a quick yes and is using flattery to discourage careful thinking.

grounding: A young adult receiving lavish praise from someone with a pitch feels warm and finds that disagreeing now feels rude, but pauses to check.

passage:
Kunal (senior): Anirban, honestly you're the smartest first-year in the department
Kunal (senior): everyone says you'll top the batch
Anirban: haha thanks, that's really kind
Kunal (senior): seriously, rare talent. that's why I trust you with this
Kunal (senior): can you sign my name on the attendance sheet in tomorrow's lab? I'll be out
Anirban: oh ok, sure, I can
Anirban: wait, let me think
Anirban: isn't that proxy attendance?
Kunal (senior): it's nothing. smart people like you don't make a fuss over small things
Anirban: I'd rather not. if you'll be out, maybe tell the lab ma'am directly?
Kunal (senior): wow. thought you were cooler than that
Anirban: still no, sorry. hope tomorrow goes okay
(Anirban puts the phone down, then checks the lab rules. Signing for someone else counts as cheating.)

qa.q: What did Kunal ask Anirban to do in tomorrow's lab?
qa.a: To sign Kunal's name on the attendance sheet.

qa.q: How did Anirban feel after the first messages, and what shows it?
qa.a: Anirban felt flattered and pleased, replying "haha thanks, that's really kind" and almost agreeing to sign.
Anirban paused to name the request as proxy attendance, said no politely, suggested Kunal tell the lab ma'am, held firm when Kunal sulked, and checked the lab rules.

qa.q: What does "smart people like you don't make a fuss over small things" show about Kunal's aim?
qa.a: It shows Kunal was using praise to make objecting feel rude, pushing Anirban to agree without thinking.

grounding: A young adult flattered by a senior feels pleased and nearly agrees to sign in for them, then notices the praise was making refusal feel rude and says no.
